name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,385

clue.text: Lay a charge against heartless trooper from the east

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its central letter
in an across clue, coming from the east means reading from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone files a complaint about a soldier who behaved callously, arriving from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: TROOPER has seven letters; dropping the middle O leaves TROPER, which read right to left is REPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: To report someone to the authorities is to make a formal complaint or accusation about them.

clue.text: Sally in tears over ring found by a couple from Tenby

indicators.note: one thing sitting inside another, here the ring placed within the word for tears
a couple means two, so only the opening pair of letters of the town is taken
found beside means simply placed next to what came before

blocks.note: rips are tears in cloth
O is ring-shaped
first two letters of the Welsh seaside town

explanation.surface: A weeping person called Sally wears a ring found by a pair of visitors to a Welsh resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name but is the definition: a sally is a witty retort.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty reply, and a riposte is exactly such a sharp comeback in conversation.

clue.text: Ancient priest, following an example, volunteers to quit

indicators.note: one part comes after the other in the order of the answer
whatever quits leaves, so those letters are taken out of the word

blocks.note: PR is a standard abbreviation for priest
following an example is being imitative
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: An elderly priest copies others' good example while some volunteers resign.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve; its two letters leave the word for copying, which then follows the priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive can describe something from earliest times, belonging to an early stage of history.

clue.text: Rank outsiders from Ireland managed to overcome City earlier

indicators.note: outsiders are the letters on the outside edges, first and last only
in a down entry, overcoming means sitting on top of, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: ran a business means managed it
C is the abbreviation for city
first and last letters of the country

explanation.surface: Irish long shots managed to beat City in an earlier match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank outsiders' reads as a racing phrase, but 'Rank' is the definition, meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank and rancid both describe food or smells that are stale, sour and offensive.

clue.text: Government to move quickly following princess's loss of reputation

indicators.note: the remaining parts come after the royal's name in the answer

blocks.note: Di, the late Princess of Wales, with the possessive 's
G is an abbreviation for government
to race is to move fast

explanation.surface: A government hurries after a princess has lost her good name.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is the familiar name of Diana, Princess of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgrace is the state of having lost honour, respect and public standing.

clue.text: Assistant's first to get to the bottom of plan

indicators.text: first to get to the bottom of
indicators.note: the opening letter travels down to the end, as this is a down entry

blocks.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: An assistant is first to get to the root of a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Assistant's' is 'is': AIDE's first letter is moved to the bottom, giving IDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a scheme or intended course of action, as in having an idea for the weekend.

clue.text: Deliveries of nuts seen outside front of grocer's

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter only
the slang word lies around the outside of the single letter

blocks.note: goolies is British slang for testicles, also called nuts
first letter

explanation.surface: Bags of nuts are delivered and seen outside a grocer's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A googly is a cricket delivery from a leg-spin bowler that turns the opposite way to the one expected.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket every ball bowled is a delivery, and googlies are a deceptive kind of spin ball.

clue.text: Belonging to the most famous group in Portugal is terrific

definitions.text: Belonging to the most famous group

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of one word, the next whole word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Being in Portugal's most celebrated set is a wonderful thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-list is the top tier of celebrities, so an A-list star belongs to the most famous group.

clue.text: Charm offensive finally has Italian running back to engage you in conversation

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word
spoken out loud, the pronoun sounds like a single letter
going back means the word is read from end to start
engaging something means taking it in, so the reversed word holds the pronoun
the ending of the first word possesses the rest, which follows it

blocks.note: last letter
a Roman is an Italian from Rome
the letter U is said exactly like the pronoun

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking Italian on a charm offensive comes back to chat you up.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour someone is to captivate or charm them so that they fall in love.

clue.text: Place firmly in position to keep top of it from bending easily

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter alone
keeping something means holding it within, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: to plant something is to set it firmly in place
first letter

explanation.surface: Fixing something securely stops it from flexing at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant describes a material that is supple and flexible, giving way without breaking.

clue.text: Flower girl

blocks.note: first meaning: a plant, also called speedwell, with small blue blooms
second meaning: a woman's first name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower girl' reads as a bridesmaid at a wedding, but the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant genus speedwell is botanically named so, and the same word is a common female forename.

clue.text: Considered action to take over club

indicators.note: taking something over here means absorbing it inside

blocks.note: a deed is an act
a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: Members weighed up a move to take control of their club.
explanation.definitionFit: To have debated something is to have thought it over or weighed the arguments for it.

clue.text: Lively pair oddly attending religious ceremony in Swaziland

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters only, the first and third
attending here means accompanying, so the two parts sit side by side
the combined pieces are placed inside the country code

blocks.note: SD was Swaziland's international vehicle registration code
letters 1 and 3
a rite is a solemn ceremony

explanation.surface: A couple bring energy to a church service in southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Swaziland (now Eswatini) used SD on its international car plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirited means full of energy, enthusiasm and determination, much the same as lively.

clue.text: Drunk with Bangladesh's opener before game

indicators.note: an opener is the first item, so the first letter is meant
the single letter is placed ahead of the next part

blocks.note: first letter
lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: A Bangladeshi opening batsman got drunk before the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests a cricket opener, but it only picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is informal British slang for extremely intoxicated by alcohol.

clue.text: Feel better about having insurance

blocks.note: re means concerning
insurance provides cover

explanation.surface: You feel happier knowing you have an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to get well again after illness, which is to start to feel better.

clue.text: Leave the centre of Exeter around eleven

indicators.note: only the middle letters of the city's name are kept
the middle pair is split so that it goes round the numeral

blocks.note: middle two letters
XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Depart from Exeter city centre at around eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around eleven' sounds like a time of day, but eleven is the Roman numeral XI.
explanation.definitionFit: Exit as a verb means to go out or depart, so it can replace leave.

clue.text: English international returns to face me, the one out in front

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read in the other direction
facing something means standing in front of it, so this part goes first

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a player capped for their country is a cap
the crossword's compiler refers to themselves

explanation.surface: An England player comes back to confront the speaker, who is now in the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus CAP turned round gives PACE, placed before SETTER. 'Me' meaning the setter is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacesetter leads a race or a field, setting the speed for everyone behind.

clue.text: Stop for a short time after queen enters gallery

indicators.note: the brief period follows the royal letters
to enter is to go inside, so these letters go into the gallery

blocks.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery
ER, Elizabeth Regina
min is short for minute

explanation.surface: Halt briefly once the monarch walks into the art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) stands for the Queen; the Tate is London's best-known gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to bring it to an end, or to stop it.

clue.text: First-rate crack

blocks.note: first meaning: of the highest quality
second meaning: expert, highly skilled, as a crack shot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a noun, a split or fissure, but it is the adjective for an expert; read literally the answer is also a notch at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes excellence, as do both words: superior quality and elite skill.

clue.text: Old fellows against backing Penny, a female prodigy

indicators.note: backing means coming behind, so these pieces follow the coin and the bird

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
a hen is a female bird
O is a standard abbreviation for old
fellows are men
leaning on something is leaning against it

explanation.surface: Elderly men oppose supporting a woman called Penny, a gifted girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name but is the coin abbreviation P.
explanation.definitionFit: A phenomenon can be a remarkable person, especially a child of exceptional talent or ability.

clue.text: Misconstrue part involving clergyman supporting soldiers in revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so these letters are read backwards
involving means holding within, so the outer abbreviation wraps the rest

blocks.note: pt is the abbreviation for part
Rev, short for Reverend
the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A vicar backing troops in an uprising twists the meaning of something.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) is a common crossword name for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To pervert words is to distort their meaning, interpreting them wrongly on purpose.

clue.text: Attempt to secure rector's support

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside

blocks.note: to have a pop at something is to have a go
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: Someone tries to win the backing of the parish rector.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is something that holds another thing up, a physical or moral support.

clue.text: Endless nonsense about limit of understanding

indicators.note: with no end, the word loses its final letter
about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round the rest

blocks.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or nonsense
to tie someone down is to limit or restrict them

explanation.surface: Endless rubbish talk pushes someone to the end of their tolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British slang for something worthless or untrue; 'limit of understanding' looks like one phrase, but 'understanding' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone patient is tolerant and forbearing, as is an understanding person.

clue.text: Cancel industrial action

blocks.note: first meaning: to delete or cross out
second meaning: a walkout by workers

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests calling off a walkout; the two parts instead define one word separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike out a line is to delete it, and a stoppage by workers withdrawing labour is a strike.

clue.text: Be fretful long after area is shelled

indicators.note: a shelled word has lost its outer casing, its first and last letters
the yearning word comes after the remaining letters

blocks.note: middle letters
to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: People yearn for peace once a district has been bombarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelled' suggests artillery fire, but it means stripped of its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to be discontented or complain and fret about one's lot.

clue.text: Vexation shown by extremely perverse girl

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters
Eve, a girl's name

explanation.surface: A very contrary girl causes annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeve is a source of irritation or annoyance, as in a pet peeve.

clue.text: Hesitation over standing by exact limit

indicators.note: turned over, so the hesitation sound is written backwards
standing next to means simply set alongside

blocks.note: er is the sound of hesitating
strict means precise, exact

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over sticking to a precise boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict is to keep within bounds, to confine or limit something.

clue.text: Former PM heading off for a place of seclusion

indicators.note: with the head removed, the name loses its first letter

blocks.note: Tony Blair, UK Prime Minister 1997-2007

explanation.surface: An ex-Prime Minister sets off to a quiet retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is Prime Minister, Britain's head of government.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a den or hideaway, a private retreat where someone hides away.

clue.text: Happening at university to almost everyone after a time

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: an event is a happening
U is the abbreviation for university
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Something at college happens to nearly everybody sooner or later.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual describes what comes about in the end, at some later point, rather than immediately.

clue.text: Fish brought back recently get spread out

indicators.note: bringing something back turns it round so it reads the other way

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, often spelt id
late means of recent times, as in 'of late'

explanation.surface: Fish recently brought back home get laid out on display.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate is to become wider or larger, as pupils expand in darkness.

clue.text: Garment from River Island splitting time and time again

indicators.note: splitting means coming between, so the letter breaks into the word

blocks.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
hr is short for hour, a time
I is the abbreviation for island
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A garment from River Island, the British high-street fashion chain, bought over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: River Island is a UK clothing retailer, which hides the river and island split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee shirt is a simple collarless short-sleeved top, an everyday piece of clothing.

clue.text: Exclusive religious group embracing the essence of self

indicators.note: the essence is the core, so the middle letters are taken
to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so the group goes round

blocks.note: a sect is a religious faction
middle two letters

explanation.surface: An elite cult keeps the core of the self close.
explanation.definitionFit: Select describes something chosen for quality and open only to a privileged few.
